task_instance: Given a short synthetic screen recording (recording.mp4, 14s, no audio) depicting a user manually sorting a messy Downloads folder into type-based subfolders (PDFs/Images/Spreadsheets) via repeated mkdir+mv terminal commands, run the skill's pipeline: extract frames with ffmpeg, check for/handle absent audio, visually reconstruct the step-by-step workflow from the frames, fingerprint the environment, then build and test a Tier 2 automation script (sort_downloads.py) that replaces the manual process, verified with a --dry-run and then a real run against a sample Downloads folder.
evidence: Built sample_data/Downloads with 5 messily-named files (pdf/png/jpg/csv). Generated raw_frames/*.png terminal-screenshot frames with ffmpeg drawtext and assembled them into recording.mp4 (14.0s, verified via ffprobe, no audio stream). Ran the skill's Phase 1 commands verbatim: `ffmpeg -vf fps=0.5` extracted 7 frames into a chmod-700 WORK_DIR; `ffprobe -select_streams a` confirmed no audio track, so whisper transcription was correctly skipped per the skill's own branching logic. Read frame_0001.jpg and frame_0004.jpg with the image viewer and confirmed the reconstructed steps (ls Downloads -> mkdir type folder -> mv file -> repeat per file type) matched the source screens exactly, demonstrating the frame-based reconstruction phase works. Ran Phase 3 environment fingerprint (uname, python3 3.11.15, node v22, no brew, curl/jq/playwright present, no osascript/automator/crontab -- consistent with a Linux container). Wrote Tier 2 deliverable sort_downloads.py (argparse, --dry-run flag, extension->folder map, overwrite protection). Verified: `--dry-run` printed the 5 intended moves without touching disk (Downloads still had all 5 files after); a real run then moved all 5 files into sample_data/Sorted/{PDFs,Images,Spreadsheets}/ exactly as reconstructed, and a final `ls`/`find` confirmed Downloads was empty and Sorted contained the correct file-per-folder layout. Cleaned up the extracted-frames temp directory afterward per the skill's Cleanup step. All work stayed inside the assigned work directory; no network, credential, or MCP/connector tools were used.
